reviews.title: Requires pristine sheet music
reviews.text:
I have many .pdf music scores.  However, after paying for the app, I discovered that my files are not high enough quality to use.  They do not properly play back…only a random note. Also, to import a photo, you cannot lay sheet music horizontal, as on a table.  You have to hold it vertically.  Awkward. You need to know this about pdf’s and/or using a photo taken from another screen (from their troubleshooting file): 

If results are poor, the problem us usually something to do with the image.

For music captured with the camera see Camera help above
Screenshots and especially direct photos of another screen will give poor results.  Use the original paper music or of PDF score
Some PDF scores are too low resolution or poor quality for optical recognition.  Most music can be obtained in full resolution.  This includes virtually all commercially published music.  See Creating a Playable PDF above
JPG images must be high resolution.  If a JPG is less than 1.5 Megabytes it is probably low resolution
Scans should be made at 300DPI.  Scans below 300DPI may lack sufficient detail.  We don’t recommend scanning at a higher DPI than 300

reviews.title: Worst presentation
reviews.text:
I spent nearly an hour troubleshooting why my PDF scores wouldn’t import — restarting the iPad, reinstalling the app, checking permissions — only to eventually discover (deep in the Help section) that PDF import requires a Professional subscription.

This wasn’t made clear during the import process. Instead of simply stating that a subscription is required, the app greys out files without explanation. That creates unnecessary confusion and wasted time.

Please make subscription limitations clearly visible at the moment a user attempts to import a PDF. It would greatly improve the user experience.

reviews.title: Why doesn’t it work anymore?
reviews.text:
Last year, I paid for a month long subscription so that I could scan all my choir music for Lent and Easter and share practice tracks with choir members. It worked great then, although I did have to recapture pages a number of times to get them to play properly. Now I have paid for another month subscription to do the same for this year’s music. I haven’t even gotten through two pages of the first song, and I’m ready to give up… I’ve captured page one dozens of times, in different lighting, at different angles, you name it, and it refuses to play back properly! How do I get my money back?

UPDATE: No, the music is not handwritten, it is normal SATB choir music, and the pictures are very high quality, captured with a brand new iPhone 17 pro. Perhaps I am forgetting just how long it took me to get decent recordings for last year’s songs. I did find that I had better luck with my music lying flat, contrary to the advice that the app constantly flashed on screen. Also, taking the photos with my phone’s camera app and then uploading them into PlayScore cut down on having to recapture pages by probably 90% over using the in-app camera. I now have *mostly* usable recordings, but there are certain areas of my songs that still don’t sound right. It seems to have a lot of trouble with key changes and various other notations. My review stands. The user experience is incredibly frustrating and time consuming.
